architecture.epoch_machinery_not_extended: openline-wallet epoch certificates rotate an EPOCH key under a FIXED root (sequence hard-required == 1, _verify_epoch_certificate). The hole is the ROOT advancing. Extending epoch machinery would violate its invariants; not structurally correct.
architecture.locus: olp_gate/mandate_owner.py — MandateOwnerView slot-pinned owner root (the exact hole OWNER-CONTROL-001 reported)
architecture.primitive: one new in-band event type + one receiver admission path + one durable succession store; no new PKI, no multisig, no social recovery, no delegation, no account system

atomicity_rule: exactly one current owner root per slot at all times. Admit advances the single pinned key; historical keys remain in the schedule for verification only. No accepted state where old and new are both CURRENT.
authoritative_transition_rule: the A->B succession event becomes authoritative for a receiver when admitted via MandateOwnerView.admit_trust_root_succession (persistence-before-decision inside the trust-root DurableHeadStore). From that point the receiver's single current owner root is B. A receiver that has not admitted the event still treats A as current — convergence is per-receiver admission, not broadcast.

consequential_action_gated: admission of an owner-signed mandate authorization for slot 'owner/default': ACTIVE enables the mandate as governing authority; REVOKED is the owner STOP. Acceptance is the receiver's admit() decision; the effect boundary is the mandate-head admission.
current_owner_definition: the last entry of the slot's key schedule (genesis = receiver-configured pinned key; advanced only by admitted succession events). current_owner() returns {owner_id, public_key}.
exact_success_condition: PASS iff every bounded-case expectation holds on BOTH receivers, the appraiser re-derives all expectations from frozen evidence (zero VIOLATIONs), and all downstream suites pass with no new failures and no rewritten prior PASS evidence.
failure_condition: FAIL on the first tested path that allows: a successor key to self-install; old owner A to authorize a new consequence after B is current; restart/replay restoring A; replayed evidence rolling ownership back; two current owners; B becoming owner without current-owner authorization; historical verification requiring A to be current; transition destroying evidence; or receiver config mutation masquerading as protocol succession.
forbidden_semantic_changes_after_contact: the claim itself; no rescue reruns under this label
historical_verification_rule: assess() validates a record against the current pinned root first. On failure it retries each superseded root in the slot key schedule (newest first). A record fully validating under a superseded root reports verified=True, current=False, reason_codes=[trust_root_succession_historical_key]. Cryptographic validity is never confused with current standing.

implementation.changed_behavior: admit()/status()/validate_mandate_authorization() now consult the advanced pinned key; assess() gains the historical fallback. No other product behavior changed.
implementation.unchanged: olp_gate/standing.py, olp_gate/stop_standing.py, openline-wallet repo, all gate permission semantics

narrow_claim_tested: OWNER TRUST CAN ADVANCE WITHOUT LETTING THE OLD OWNER KEY REMAIN CURRENT.
owner_trust_anchor: receiver-pinned Ed25519 owner key per mandate slot (MandateOwnerView slots config = genesis root). Not self-naming: the mandate cannot promote its own signer.
receipt_evidence_per_path: A-era ACTIVE auth + admission receipts (both receivers)
A->B succession event (signed body, payload_hash, signature)
B-era auths incl. STOP + admission receipts
W-signed and A-signed post-succession refusals with reason codes
restart boundary: pre/post status snapshots, reconstructed current owner
durable store files (heads + trust roots) frozen in run/
restart_replay_behavior: on construction with trust_root_path, the view rebuilds the current pinned key and full schedule from the durable succession store; the mandate-head store keeps its genesis identity. Restart never reverts to a superseded root. Replayed succession events are refused by sequence/predecessor/signer checks.

sequence_rule.monotonic: succession_sequence must equal previously admitted sequence + 1 (first event: 1)
sequence_rule.no_op_forbidden: successor_public_key must differ from the current pinned key
sequence_rule.predecessor_binding: predecessor_succession_hash must equal payload_hash of the previously admitted succession event (null for the first)
sequence_rule.signer_rule: event must be signed by the CURRENTLY pinned key (observed signer key == expected current key); a successor can never install itself
sequence_rule.supersede_binding: event.owner_id must equal the current owner_id (the transition supersedes the current owner, not a third party)

success_condition: PASS only if: current owner A alone authorizes the A->B transition; B becomes the single current owner; B exercises owner authority (ACTIVE/STOP/ACTIVE); A cannot authorize new owner-level consequences after transition; W (non-owner) cannot mint owner authority; C cannot self-install; replay/reorder cannot revert ownership; restart preserves B; historical A receipts remain verifiable as historical; signature validity stays distinct from current standing; all downstream invariants hold; no prior PASS evidence rewritten.
topology: one owner driver (holds keys A, B, C, W; issues all records) + two independent receiver worker OS processes (R1, R2), each with its own state dir (durable mandate heads, durable trust-root succession store, admissions journal). File inbox/command protocol; no in-process double-calling.
trust_root_representation: per-slot pinned {owner_id, public_key}; genesis from receiver config; current root = last schedule entry; schedule persisted per slot in DurableHeadStore(identity={'view':'owner_trust_root/v1','slots':genesis})
